rfi.description: Ukraine's allies on Monday pledged to keep up their support in the war against Russia, with a renewed focus on air defence investment to counter a shortage of US Patriot interceptors.

rfi.description: France and Saudi Arabia on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding for a six-billion-euro ($7 billion) Saudi investment to create three theme parks near Paris, including one likely to be manga-themed, the office of the French president said.

rfi.description: A leading group monitoring and providing aid to migrants crossing the Mediterranean have warned that its rescue ships have been facing increasing threats and harassment from Libyan groups.

rfi.title: Malian PM's visit to Algeria underlines need for mutual security goals
rfi.description: The acting head of the Malian government, General Abdoulaye Maiga has begun a two-day visit to Algeria. It comes amid a thaw after months of tension. RFI spoke to Bakary Sambe, the Director of the Timbuktu Institute about the security situation and what the countries hope to gain from the meeting.

rfi.title: Six million Somalis face acute hunger as drought and conflict worsen
rfi.description: Six million people in Somalia are facing acute hunger, with nearly two million children at emergency levels, as severe drought, conflict and falling humanitarian funding deepen what the UN describes as one of the world’s worst malnutrition crises. Medical charity MSF tells RFI it's sounding the alarm "before it's too late".

rfi.title: Violence against healthcare workers in DRC hampers Ebola response
rfi.description: Healthcare workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo have been coming under attack, the United Nations and Red Cross have warned, hampering efforts to stem the spread of the Ebola virus, which is spreading 'exponentially'.

rfi.title: Centre-left Glucksmann enters French presidential race as left tries to unite
rfi.description: French centre-left politician Raphael Glucksmann has announced his candidacy for next year's presidential election, seeking to challenge hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon to lead France's fractured left, as a campaign increasingly dominated by the far right takes shape.

rfi.title: Scorching summer takes toll on bees and honey harvests in France
rfi.description: France produces 20,000 tonnes of honey each year, but successive heatwaves and persistent drought across Europe this summer are impacting bee populations as flowering plants dry out and colonies struggle to find food. Beekeeper Romain Lacotte and his family farm 1,000 hives in Haute-Corrèze, central France, an area considered one of the country's natural water towers. But even there, he tells RFI, high temperatures and lack of rain are taking their toll.

rfi.title: DRC and M23 rebels agree on roadmap for peace in eastern Congo
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo government and the M23 rebel group have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks aimed at resolving the protracted conflict in eastern DRC. It marks the latest step in an internationally brokered peace process that has seen the parties make cautious concessions, without ending the fighting.

rfi.title: Saudi crown prince heads to France as Paris seeks closer Gulf ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Sunday for a two-day official visit, as Paris looks to deepen ties with Riyadh against a backdrop of war in the Middle East.

rfi.title: Mystery elephant deaths in Kenya leave experts divided over cause
rfi.description: Conservationists and Maasai communities are calling for urgent answers as paralysis-like symptoms spread among elephants in Kenya's Amboseli National Park, with competing theories emerging over what is causing their deaths.

rfi.title: Togo says it has 'serious' evidence against detained French journalists
rfi.description: Togo's government says it has "serious and consistent evidence" against two French documentary filmmakers detained since July on charges of making false statements. Gaël Mocaër and Sebastian Perez Pezzani were arrested along with their Togolese fixer, Fred Vedomey, and have denied wrongdoing.

rfi.title: Southern African mothers plead for sons lured to Russia's war in Ukraine
rfi.description: Instead of celebrating her son's birthday this month, Zimbabwean mother Rodwin Chitewere spent the day praying for his body to be brought home from Russia, where he was reportedly killed fighting Moscow's war against Ukraine.

rfi.title: Eroding coastlines unearth and destroy slave graves in French Caribbean
rfi.description: Rising seas and coastal erosion are exposing the graves of enslaved people on beaches in the French Caribbean departments of Martinique and Guadeloupe, bringing long-buried remains back into view. Archaeologists say the retreating coastline is revealing new information about people who were enslaved centuries ago, but also destroying sites of historical and cultural importance.

rfi.title: Ravaged by wildfires, France's Fontainebleau forest reopens to public
rfi.description: The forest of Fontainebleau outside Paris has partially reopened to the public after remaining off-limits for over a month due to devastating wildfires. From Saturday, visitors can access some 80 percent of the forest, but are being warned to show caution around fragile wildlife and charred trees.

rfi.title: Still waters run deep: why Palme d'or winner 'Fjord' questions our certainties
rfi.description: An isolated village in Norway sees its peaceful veneer upset by the arrival of a new family in Fjord, the Palme d'Or-winning film released in French cinemas this week. Inspired by real-life cases, Romanian director Cristian Mungiu explores questions of domestic violence, religion, culture and tolerance through a story that asks whose version of the truth can be trusted.

rfi.title: Diplomats urge France and UK to uphold rule of law in Palestinian territories
rfi.description: Dozens of former senior French and UK diplomats on Saturday urged their governments to work together to uphold international law in the Palestinian territories, accusing Israel of seeking to "destroy" any prospect of a viable Palestinian state.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : les drones russes traquent les civils, les "safaris humains" se multiplient
france24fr.description: La vidéo d’un cycliste ukrainien ciblé par un drone posté vendredi par l’armée russe puis dépubliée a suscité un vif émoi en ligne. Ce n’est pourtant pas la première fois que les opérateurs de drones russes sont accusés de terroriser les civils ukrainiens en les prenant pour cible. Des “safaris humains” qualifiés de "crime contre l’humanité" par l’ONU.

france24fr.title: Un feu de forêt dans le Nevada pousse des dizaines de milliers de personnes à évacuer
france24fr.description: L'incendie "Hawk Fire", d'origine humaine, a déjà ravagé plus de 6 000 hectares dans le Nevada où il menace la ville de Reno. Les écoles ont été fermées lundi et des dizaines milliers de personnes ont reçu l'ordre d'évacuer. Si aucun mort n'est à déplorer pour l'instant, on dénombre sept blessés, dont trois secouristes.

france24fr.title: "Nuit de terreur" en Haïti : une quarantaine de personnes tuées dans une attaque de gangs
france24fr.description: Dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi, des membres de gangs ont attaqué un camp de déplacés situé dans une église à Kenscoff, dans les hauteurs de la capitale haïtienne Port-au-Prince. Une quarantaine de cadavres ont été recensés et certaines personnes ont été enlevées, selon le maire de la commune.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis retirent la Syrie de leur liste des pays accusés de soutenir le terrorisme
france24fr.description: Washington a franchi lundi une nouvelle étape dans la levée des sanctions contre la Syrie en retirant le pays de la liste des soutiens au terrorisme. Cette mesure "élimine les derniers obstacles majeurs à l'investissement du secteur privé en Syrie et favorise la reprise économique du pays ainsi que sa réintégration dans l'économie mondiale", a indiqué le secrétaire d'État Marco Rubio.

france24fr.title: Benjamin Netanyahu assure que l'Iran a "essayé de tuer" l'un de ses deux fils
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu a affirmé lundi, lors d'un entretien téléphonique avec la chaîne Channel 14, que l'Iran avait pris pour cible l'un de ses fils, sans donner plus de précisions. Selon le journaliste Amit Segal, cette tentative d'assassinat présumée était connue depuis "des mois" mais faisait l'objet d'une interdiction de publication.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : la riposte sur le fleuve Congo
france24fr.description: En République démocratique du Congo, la progression du virus Ebola inquiète. Partie d’une seule province, elle en touche désormais six. Et face à cette propagation fulgurante, un autre front se dessine : celui du fleuve Congo. Véritable artère du pays, le fleuve transporte chaque jour des milliers de passagers et de marchandises et pourrait aussi devenir une voie de circulation du virus. Reportage d'Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula au port de Bende Bende, aux abords de Kinshasa.

france24fr.title: La "Coalition des volontaires" réaffirme son soutien à Volodymyr Zelensky
france24fr.description: À l'occasion du 35e anniversaire de l'indépendance de l'Ukraine, le président Zelensky a salué, lundi, la résilience de son peuple après plus de quatre ans de guerre. La "Coalition des volontaires", co-présidée par le Premier ministre britannique, s'est réunie virtuellement en présence d'Emmanuel Macron et du chancelier allemand, Friedrich Merz.

france24fr.title: Comment les États-Unis comptent "asphyxier l'économie" de l'Iran
france24fr.description: Lors d’une conférence de presse à Washington, le secrétaire au Trésor, Scott Bessent, a présenté, lundi, un nouveau train de sanctions contre l’Iran visant l’or, la technologie, les actifs numériques, l’aviation et le transport maritime. Il a également adressé un avertissement ferme aux pays qui continueraient à soutenir Téhéran.

france24fr.title: Une tornade ravage le village de Pomas dans le sud de la France
france24fr.description: Le village de Pomas, dans l'Aude, a été ravagé lundi par une tornade qui a blessé des dizaines de personnes et frappé 300 habitations. De nombreuses toitures ont été arrachées et des maisons soufflées.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : le festival Kin'Act fête ses 10 ans
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 À Kinshasa en RDC, le festival Kin’Act célèbre ses 10 ans. L'événement met à l’honneur des performeurs habillés de créations spectaculaires fabriquées à partir de déchets recyclés. Devenus emblématiques dans les rues de la capitale, ils alertent sur l’insalubrité dans la ville.

france24fr.title: Soudan : la crise alimentaire s’aggrave face à la sécheresse
france24fr.description: Une forte sécheresse menace les cultures au Soudan, notamment dans le sud-est du pays.Un nouveau coup dur pour les agriculteurs, alors que la guerre a plongé le pays dans l’une des pires crises alimentaires au monde.

france24fr.title: Près de Paris, l'Arabie saoudite va financer trois parcs d'attractions
france24fr.description: L'Arabie saoudite a signé, lundi, un protocole d'accord avec la France pour créer trois parcs d'attractions en région parisienne, dont l'un probablement sur l'univers des mangas. Le projet d'investissement saoudien de six milliards d'euros, présenté comme "sans précédent" par Emmanuel Macron, doit aussi permettre de créer 22 000 emplois directs.

france24fr.title: Le maire LFI de Saint-Denis Bally Bagayoko visé par une enquête pour détournement de fonds publics
france24fr.description: Le Parquet national financier a ouvert une enquête pour "détournement de fonds publics, recel et concussion" sur le maire insoumis de Saint-Denis Bally Bagayoko. Les enquêteurs cherchent à comprendre les conditions de son emploi à la RATP alors qu'il exerçait des mandats d'élu. L'édile dénonce des accusations "non fondées", tandis que La France insoumise fustige une "cabale" politique.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Les États-Unis dévoilent de nouvelles sanctions visant à "couper toutes les sources de revenus" de l'Iran
Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann veut remporter la primaire socialiste sur une ligne anti-LFI
france24fr.description: Raphaël Glucksmann, désormais candidat à la primaire socialiste, a fait du rapport de la gauche à Jean-Luc Mélenchon et de la question d’une éventuelle alliance avec La France insoumise aux législatives de 2027 un élément central de son projet politique en vue des débats à venir face à ses concurrents.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: In der Walliser Gemeinde Randa droht ein Gletscherabbruch
LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Trump gratuliert der Ukraine zum Unabhängigkeitstag +++ Die Ukraine hat eine Ölraffinerie in Krasnodar angegriffen
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Dies sind die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Ein Flugzeug der Swiss setzt über dem Atlantik einen Notruf ab – Radardaten zeigen ein Landemanöver über den Azoren
nzz.description: Die Maschine ist auf der Insel Terceira gelandet. Über die Hintergründe der Notlandung ist noch nichts bekannt.

nzz.title: Ein Brand im amerikanischen Gliedstaat Nevada hat ein Dutzend Häuser zerstört
nzz.description: Die Feuerwehr meldet Fortschritte im Kampf gegen einen Flächenbrand am Rand der Stadt Reno. Doch einige Anwohner haben ihre Häuser verloren.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Krise in Syrien: USA streicht Syrien von Liste der Terrorunterstützer
nzz.description: Seit dem Sturz des langjährigen Machthabers Bashar al-Asad Ende 2024 erlebt Syrien ungewisse Zeiten. So zeigt sich zurzeit die Lage.

nzz.title: Erste Daten der FMH zu Taxpunkt-Deckel: Nur 7 Prozent der Ärzte sind betroffen
nzz.description: Der Unmut in der Ärzteschaft ist gross. Sie dürfen ab 2027 für gewisse Behandlungen nur noch eine maximale Anzahl Taxpunkte verrechnen. Eine Analyse des Verbands FMH zeigt: Ein Grossteil der Ärzte bleibt bereits heute unter der vorgesehenen Limite.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Das Kunsthaus sollte kostenbewusster denken, statt mit der Schliessung von Räumen zu drohen. Dennoch braucht es die Unterstützung der Stadt Zürich
nzz.description: Im Vergleich mit anderen kulturellen Institutionen der Stadt steht das Museum gut da. Es muss sich aber mehr anstrengen, um in die schwarzen Zahlen zu kommen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Hammer, Sichel, Sünneli – die missbrauchte Friedenstaube
nzz.description: Christoph Blocher wirbt für seine Neutralitätsinitiative mit einer schneeweissen Friedenstaube. Doch Russland nutzt die Taube schon seit einem halben Jahrhundert für seine Zwecke – und das sieht man Blochers Gefolgschaft an.

nzz.title: Kanadier sind zäh. Das beweist Premierminister Mark Carney im Handelsstreit mit den USA
nzz.description: Ausgerechnet der ehemalige Banker will Donald Trump zeigen, dass Geld nicht alles ist.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Umbruch bei VW: was in den kommenden Tagen zu erwarten ist
nzz.description: Der VW-Chef Oliver Blume will den Konzern radikal umbauen, um ihn zukunftsfähig zu machen. Die Belegschaft äussert Kritik. Anfang September dürften erste Entscheide gefällt werden.

nzz.title: Kanada bricht die Zollverhandlungen mit den USA ab – wäre das auch für die Schweiz eine Option?
nzz.description: Kanada hat als erstes Land seit langem den Verhandlungstisch mit den USA verlassen. Nun steuern die beiden Länder auf einen Handelskrieg zu. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Heiss ersehnte Spaghetti oder heissersehnte Spagetti? Vor dreissig Jahren wurde die grosse Rechtschreibreform beschlossen. Jetzt wird zurückbuchstabiert
nzz.description: Das neueste Regelwerk zur deutschen Rechtschreibung zeigt: Reformer und Rechtschreibräte sind auf dem ungeordneten Rückmarsch. Sie geben das Rückwärts für ein Vorwärts aus und wenden ihre eigenen Regeln nicht richtig an.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Gewerkschaften verlangen eine 13. Pensionskassenrente: Das ist eine Schnapsidee
nzz.description: Die Forderung einer «Dreizehnten» in der beruflichen Vorsorge wirkt absurd: Rechnerisch ginge dies nur dann auf, wenn die künftigen Pensionäre weniger lang lebten.

nzz.title: Tesla drängt auf den Markt für Robotaxis: mit Cybercabs ohne Lenkrad und Pedale
nzz.description: Amerika nähert sich der fahrerlosen Zukunft: Die neuen Cybercabs von Tesla könnten schon im August Passagiere durch Austin transportieren. Dabei setzt die Firma auf eine andere Strategie als ihre Konkurrenten.

nzz.title: Strategie gegen Russland: Wie Polen sein Volk wehrhaft macht – und was die Schweiz daraus lernen kann
nzz.description: Nicht nur die Armee, die gesamte Gesellschaft soll der Bedrohung aus Russland trotzen können: Polen bereitet seine Zivilbevölkerung systematisch auf den Ernstfall vor. Eine neue Studie empfiehlt das Modell zur Nachahmung.

nzz.title: Vorbild Trump? Im Kampf gegen Chinas Subventionsflut wird in Brüssel der Ruf nach höheren Zöllen lauter
nzz.description: Zitronensäure steckt in Süsswaren und Shampoos. Staatlich subventionierte Hersteller aus China setzen Europas Firmen in diesem Geschäft unter Druck. Welche Folgen das für Europa hat, zeigt der Besuch in einer belgischen Industriestadt.

zeit.title: Automobilkonzern: Lies sieht Werksschließungen bei VW weiter kritisch
Vor dem Liga-Start: Wer wird deutscher Meister? Das sagen die Trainer
Gamescom: Party aus Prinzip
zeit.description: Auf der Spielemesse Gamescom feiert die Branche sich und ihre Fans. Obwohl es ihr gar nicht mal so gut geht. Und ein prominenter Partygast fehlt.

Großeinsatz am See: Autofahrer schwimmt Polizeikontrolle davon - Lebenszeichen
Bargeldloses Bezahlen: Girocard mit Rekordzahlen - kontaktlos boomt
Baden-Württemberg: Verdacht auf Sabotage: Kabel an Bahnstrecke beschädigt
Unfall in Löhne: Tödlicher Unfall: 13-jährige Radfahrerin von Lkw überrollt
Verkehrsunfall: Vorfahrt genommen: Rollerfahrerin stirbt in Klinik
Weinende Männer in der Kunst: »Man sieht diese rasende Männlichkeit, und dann weint der!«
zeit.description: Der Hamburger Kunsthistoriker Philip Schinkel erforscht weinende Männer in der Kunst des 19. Jahrhunderts. Wer ihn auf das Thema brachte? Der Teufel, ausgerechnet.

zeit.title: Lohnentwicklung: Tariflöhne steigen wohl stärker als Preise
zeit.description: Die Tariflöhne in Deutschland dürften laut einer Berechnung dieses Jahr stärker steigen als die Verbraucherpreise. Wichtige Tarifrunden stehen allerdings noch bevor.

zeit.title: Hochbegabung am Arbeitsplatz : Wenn es schadet, zu intelligent zu sein
zeit.description: Hochbegabte haben nicht nur Vorteile im Job – im Gegenteil. Oft provozieren sie Missverständnisse und Neid. Was diese Menschen brauchen, um ihr Potenzial zu entfalten.

zeit.title: Ukrainekarte aktuell: Ukrainer vertreiben Angreifer bei Slowjansk, Huljajpole und Orichiw
zeit.description: Der russische Vorstoß in Richtung Slowjansk ist bei Dibrowa zurückgedrängt worden. Bei Huljajpole haben ukrainische Soldaten zwei Dörfer von Sturmtruppen befreit.

zeit.title: Nina Warken: Kanzleramtschefin sieht Regierung nach Sommerpause vor großen Aufgaben
zeit.description: Vor der Kabinettsklausur in Neuhardenberg spricht Nina Warken von einer langen »To-Do-Liste« der Koalition. Bei der Umsetzung von Reformen sieht sie »Luft nach oben«.

zeit.title: DFB-Pokal: Ex-DFB-Präsident fordert hohe Bußgelder nach Krawallen bei Pokalspiel
zeit.description: Reinhard Grindel kritisiert die Ausschreitungen beim Südwest-Derby zwischen Waldhof Mannheim und dem 1. FCK deutlich. Er plädiert für Strafen, »die wirklich wehtun«.

spiegel.title: Merz-Regierung kommt zu zweitägiger Kabinettsklausur in Brandenburg zusammen
spiegel.description: Vom Tegernsee aufs Schloss Neuhardenberg: Kanzler Merz lädt sein Kabinett nach der Sommerpause zur Arbeitssitzung nach Brandenburg. Auf der To-do-Liste steht ein Reformherbst – und ein wenig Klimaschutz.

spiegel.title: BIP: Deutsche Wirtschaft wächst im zweiten Quartal stärker als gedacht
spiegel.description: Die Unterschiede sind nicht riesig, aber immerhin: Von April bis Juni gab es mehr Wachstum als zuvor angenommen. Dürre und Niedrigwasser haben sich allerdings erst später im Sommer ausgewirkt.

spiegel.title: Girocard: Kontaktlose Zahlungen erreichen Rekordniveau in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Die Girocard, auch bekannt als »EC-Karte«, wird immer häufiger zum Bezahlen an der Kasse verwendet. Bald sollen neue Funktionen den Erfolg stärken.

spiegel.title: Mette Frederiksen: Dänische Premierministerin wehrt sich gegen Kommentare zu ihrer Nase
spiegel.description: Mette Frederiksen erhält immer wieder Nachrichten zu ihrem Aussehen. Nun veröffentlicht sie den Auszug eines Chats, offenbar mit einem Schönheitschirurgen.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Jeder zwölfte Fernzug fällt im ersten Halbjahr aus
spiegel.description: Zugverspätungen sind ärgerlich – noch schlimmer ist es, wenn Züge komplett oder auf einem Teil der Strecke ausfallen. Auch in dieser Kategorie fährt die Bahn traurige Rekorde ein.

spiegel.title: Leipzig: Ermittler finden weitere Drohne und Sprengstoff am Flughafen Leipzig/Halle
spiegel.description: Zum gescheiterten Anschlag am Leipziger Flughafen gibt es nach SPIEGEL-Informationen neue Erkenntnisse. Demnach wurden eine weitere Drohne und Spuren militärischen Sprengstoffs gefunden.

spiegel.title: Spanienrundfahrt Vuelta: 3. Etappe wird nach Hagelschauer abgebrochen
spiegel.description: Superstar Tadej Pogačar hatte schon den nächsten Etappensieg bei der Spanienrundfahrt vor Augen, dann kam das Unwetter. Die Profis retteten sich vor dem Hagel ins Café, die Etappe wurde abgebrochen.

spiegel.title: Pflegeversicherung: AOK-Chefin warnt vor Acht-Milliarden-Loch ab 2027
spiegel.description: Die Kosten für die Pflege laufen aus dem Ruder. Die Vorstandschefin des AOK-Bundesverbandes warnt vor einem heftigen Defizit im kommenden Jahr und macht zwei Vorschläge, um höhere Beiträge zu vermeiden.

spiegel.title: DFB-Pokal: Schalke 04 müht sich über die Verlängerung beim Halleschen FC in die 2. Runde
spiegel.description: Es war ein mühevoller Auftakt für Schalke 04 in den DFB-Pokal dieser Saison. Der Bundesliga-Aufsteiger musste beim Halleschen FC in die Verlängerung. Auch Wolfsburg und Köln taten sich schwer.

spiegel.title: USA wollen bis zu 200.000 B-1-Geschäftsvisa und B-2-Touristenvisa aufheben
spiegel.description: Die Trump-Regierung plant eine massive Aufhebung von Visa. Sämtliche Geschäfts- und Touristenvisa sollen auf den Prüfstand. Eine Gruppe Einreisender ist besonders im Fokus.

spiegel.title: Berghütten: Warum sie ein heilsamer Ort sind, obwohl alles gegen sie spricht
spiegel.description: Enge Schlafräume, kalte Duschen, eine schmale Speisekarte. Auf dem Papier spricht wenig fürs Matratzenlager am Berg. Gerade deshalb komme ich dort zur Ruhe.

spiegel.title: ChatGPT: Desinformationskampagne aus Russland nutzte offenbar der KI von OpenAI
spiegel.description: »Deutsche Fachkräfte verlassen das sinkende Schiff«: Eine Onlinegruppierung hat offenbar eine KI verwendet, um Putin-freundliche Texte zu verbreiten. SPIEGEL-Recherchen zeigen, dass dahinter wohl ein israelischer Thinktank steckt.

spiegel.title: Volkswagen: VW-Chef Oliver Blume stellt Umbaupläne in Wolfsburg, Emden und Zwickau vor
spiegel.description: VW-Boss Oliver Blume will Europas größten Autokonzern grundlegend umbauen – und fast alle Werke in Deutschland dichtmachen. Nun muss er ausgerechnet dort für seine Pläne werben.

spiegel.title: Marlen Hobrack über Mutterschaft: Macht der Feminismus Mütter unglücklich?
Klimakrise: Grüne werfen SPD Scheinheiligkeit beim Hitzeschutz vor
spiegel.description: Die SPD will das Grundgesetz ändern, um den Hitzeschutz zu verbessern. Das stößt auf Kritik der Grünen. Der Vorwurf: Die Sozialdemokraten fordern mehr Geld für Programme, die sie zuvor selbst gekürzt haben.

spiegel.title: Outdoor-Kleidung: Welche Funktionskleidung Sie zum Laufen, Radfahren und Wandern brauchen
spiegel.description: Outdoorsportler kennen kein mieses Wetter, nur falsche Kleidung. Wie Sie die perfekte Funktionsgarderobe fürs Laufen, Radfahren oder Wandern zusammenstellen.

spiegel.title: Ultraläufe wie der Last Soul Ultra: Was hinter dem Trend steckt und wann es gefährlich wird
spiegel.description: Immer mehr Rennen und Rekorde: Backyard-Ultras über viele Tage und riesige Distanzen boomen. Beim Last Soul Ultra etwa kämpfen Läuferinnen und Läufer gegeneinander, bis nur noch einer übrig ist. Unsere Autorin war dabei.

spiegel.title: News: VW-Krise, Donald Trump, Bundeskabinett in Klausur
spiegel.description: VW-Chef Blume überbringt der Belegschaft seine Sanierungspläne. Donald Trumps Empfehlung garantiert keinen Wahlgewinn mehr. Und das Bundeskabinett macht sich Gedanken über Hitze, Wirtschaft und Arbeitsplätze. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagmorgen.

observador.title: Esquadra do Rato. Juíza dá mais mais tempo para investigar
observador.description: Ministério Público pediu mais tempo para a investigação devido à complexidade do processo e a juíza concedeu mais seis meses sem libertar os arguidos, que estão com medidas privativas de liberdade.

observador.title: Os segredos escondidos na casa do espião
observador.description: Há escadas rolantes no Metro de Lisboa avariadas há mais de três anos. O Observador foi perceber como funciona (e como está a mudar) a sua manutenção.

observador.title: Incêndios. Prisão preventiva para dois suspeitos de fogos
observador.description: Um dos homens é suspeito de ter ateado pelo menos cinco incêndios florestais em Moura Morta o outro é suspeito de ter ateado um incêndio florestal com recurso a velas de cera em Sabrosa.

observador.title: O campo invadido por um bebé e o adepto que faz jejum de ...
observador.description: De adeptos sem ir ao barbeiro há quase 700 dias a um bebé que invadiu o relvado na MLS, sobra ainda espaço para não esquecer  os percalços das marcas com publicidades infelizes.

observador.title: Hyundai Motor faz acordo salarial com sindicato após greves
observador.description: Sexta-feira, cerca de 40 mil funcionários, segundo o sindicato, da Hyundai Motor paralisaram as atividades um dia inteiro, foi a primeira greve deste tipo em dez anos, após o fracasso das negociações.

observador.title: Robô parte dentes de criança de 5 anos
observador.description: Uma criança de 5 anos perdeu quatro dentes após um "encontro" com um robô na China. A família agora exige 19 mil euros de indemnização, com medo de que a cicatriz arruine o seu futuro na polícia.

observador.title: As notícias das 8h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Quatro mortos após troca de ataques entre Ucrânia e Rússia
observador.description: Na Rússia os drones atingiram 10 casas e uma refinaria, provocando duas mortes e vários feridos. No lado ucraniano uma bomba guiada atingiu a cidade de Zaporíjia, vitimando outras duas pessoas.

observador.title: Equador. Governo acusado de tentar impedir eleições "justas"
observador.description: Vários partidos relatam tentativas do Governo de tentar "sufocar os partidos políticos da oposição", acusando-o de "jogar sujo" por medo de perder as eleições, em novembro.

observador.title: Cabrita sobre Neves: PM estabeleceu "padrão Spinumviva"
observador.description: Eduardo Cabrita entende que a postura de Luís Montenegro durante o caso Spinumviva degradou os "padrões éticos da governação" que servem aos restantes ministros do Governo.

observador.title: Luís Neves e o Governo: será preciso uma "ajuda divina"?
observador.description: Com o ministro Luís Neves em maus lençóis e a proibição da utilização das burcas a entrar em vigor, Portugal dividi-se entre crises e regras, enquanto a Europa não pode largar a Ucrânia.

observador.title: "Só o instrumento militar não chega para ganhar uma guerra"
observador.description: O tenente-general Marco Serronha diz que a opção de força militar contra o Irão voltará com tudo após as eleições nos EUA. Admite ainda que é necessário unir a diplomacia e economia para ter sucesso.

observador.title: China. Tufão Narra obrigada à retirada de 54 mil pessoas
observador.description: Tempestade afetou 61 mil pessoas na região de Guangxi, tendo 54 mil sido retiradas por prevenção. O tufão levou a que 10 rios ultrapassassem os níveis de alerta.

observador.title: Venezuela diz que já foram libertados 1.046 presos políticos
observador.description: Presidente interina prometeu respeitar a segurança dos cidadãos e garantiu um reforço do patrulhamento com métodos que respeitem os direitos humanos.

observador.title: Festival do Crato arranca com Gipsy Kings by Diego Baliardo
observador.description: Programação do Festival do Crato começa com "dia extra" de entrada gratuita com Gipsy Kings by Diego Baliardo. Calema, Slow J, Sara Correia e Calum Scott também vão subir ao palco na edição deste ano.

observador.title: Guterres condena emboscada que matou dois soldados
observador.description: Dois soldados da Etiópia foram mortos e sete ficaram feridos numa emboscada em Jonglei, no Sudão do Sul. António Guterres expressa as condolências às famílias e condena o ataque.

observador.title: EUA não estão em posição "de restringir relações comerciais"
observador.description: Irão desvaloriza o anúncio de novas sanções contra a República Islâmica, por parte dos Estados Unidos. O Presidente do Parlamento do Irão classifica como absurdas as ameaças de Donald Trump.

observador.title: China intensifica campanha anticorrupção
observador.description: Presidente Chinês instaurou, em 2013, uma forte campanha de combate à corrupção. Em 2025 foram investigados 65 altos funcionários, os quais podem ser responsabilizados mesmo após se reformarem.

letemps.title: L’immobilier, discrète vedette du rendement

letemps.title: En mer Adriatique, les grands dauphins seraient devenus dépendants des chalutiers

phys-org.title: Access to bilingual education lags behind in Andalusia's rural areas, study reveals
phys-org.description: Over the past two decades, bilingual education programs have significantly expanded within the Spanish education system, with the aim of improving foreign language learning—primarily English—while making it more accessible for all. Although more and more schools are offering bilingual education, they are unevenly distributed across the country, generating inequalities among students.

phys-org.title: Hotel stigma may drive Chinese hospitality graduates away from careers
phys-org.description: Research published in the International Journal of Environment and Sustainable Development analyzed interviews with more than 300 Chinese hotel interns to examine how perceptions of hotel work affect whether graduates pursue a career in the industry. The findings suggest that negative perceptions deter graduate interns from pursuing careers in hospitality.

phys-org.title: Process doubles the size of PFAS molecules, making them easy to destroy
phys-org.description: Ask a chemist to name the strongest single bond in organic chemistry, and they'll likely say carbon-fluorine. It's that bond, repeated dozens of times over, that gives per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) their nickname: forever chemicals. Manufacturers prize PFAS for the same reason regulators dread them. The bonds barely break down, which is exactly why the compounds are so good at repelling water, oil and heat in everything from semiconductor fabrication to nonstick cookware.

phys-org.title: What would happen to human interaction if AI could read our emotions?
phys-org.description: AI systems are increasingly being developed to recognize emotions by analyzing facial expressions, voices, body language and other physiological signals. Although the scientific validity of many of these systems remains contested, they are already being tested in health care and security settings.

phys-org.title: Blood-clotting protein may be SARS-CoV-2's hidden accomplice, helping it hide from antibodies and reach blood vessels
phys-org.description: Fibrinogen, the abundant plasma protein best known for forming blood clots, may play a second and far less benign role during SARS-CoV-2 infection: acting as a molecular bridge that simultaneously hides the virus from neutralizing antibodies and delivers it to the cells lining blood vessels.

phys-org.title: Mystery statue unearthed at Sardis archaeological dig
phys-org.description: Researchers with the long-running Harvard–Cornell Archaeological Exploration of Sardis have unearthed a larger-than-life statue estimated to be nearly 2,500 years old.

phys-org.title: Natural gas drilling could raise salt levels, in turn boosting radium in water
phys-org.description: Pennsylvania ranks second in U.S. natural gas production, accounting for about one-fifth of U.S. output in 2024, and has one of the most extensive histories of energy extraction in the country. A team of researchers from Penn State is trying to better understand the environmental impacts of these sites—specifically, whether fracking is increasing radium content in local drinking water.

phys-org.title: NASA starshade would enable astronomers to directly image rocky exoworlds
phys-org.description: A NASA-led team hopes to take a shortcut to direct imaging of extrasolar Earth-like planets. The idea is to use what they call a hybrid telescope composed of an orbital starshade coupled with the next-generation extremely large ground-based optical telescopes.

phys-org.title: Meteorite dust holds records of magnetism that may have helped form the sun
phys-org.description: Around 4.6 billion years ago, the solar system was little more than a giant ball of gas and dust. Over the next few million years, this "solar nebula" underwent a huge transformation, flattening into a disk of matter that then condensed to form the central sun and orbiting planets.

phys-org.title: How fusion reactions can survive flaws—up to a point
phys-org.description: Researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) have found that implosions designed for inertial fusion energy (IFE) can tolerate significant imperfections before performance abruptly declines, a finding that could inform the design of fuel targets for future fusion power plants.

phys-org.title: How the sun's galactic journey and superflare-filled youth shaped Earth's climate
phys-org.description: At the center of our solar system, the sun influences every planet that orbits it. In two recent studies, scientists uncovered how ancient events in the sun's history may have helped create Earth's unique climate and driven previously unexplained climatic shifts.

phys-org.title: Why marine heat waves and acidification strike together
phys-org.description: Marine heat waves and extreme ocean acidification events are each damaging on their own. But when both stressors hit simultaneously, their individual effects can be exacerbated.

phys-org.title: Supersized quantum sensors make faint photons easier to catch
phys-org.description: Our everyday life is flooded with photons, the quantum building blocks of light. For cutting-edge technology, from quantum computing to deep-tissue imaging, detecting every single photon counts.

phys-org.title: Catching cow burps in real time: Methane sensor matches industry monitor in early field test
phys-org.description: Methane is a short-lived but powerful greenhouse gas; cutting methane emissions can slow near-term warming and improve air quality by reducing harmful ground-level ozone. As ruminants digest feed, they release methane—through burps. In fact, emissions from cattle are the largest source of human-caused methane emissions (roughly 25% of the total)—so reducing emissions from cattle is an important part of tackling climate change.

phys-org.title: The midlife clock is ticking: How we understand 'time left' can help us use it well
phys-org.description: In Adaptation and the Life Cycle, psychologist Bernice Neugarten tells us that we arrive in our middle years by our social clocks, not our age.

phys-org.title: Molecular trick opens the door to a new generation of glass
phys-org.description: Researchers at TU Dortmund University, Paderborn University, the University of Duisburg-Essen, and the University of Oxford have developed a new method for selectively modifying the internal structure of specific types of glass. The study, published in the journal Nature Materials, shows how adding an organic molecule during melting causes the chemical bonds in the material to rearrange. phys-org.title: Wildlife trafficking spreads across social media, putting thousands of species at risk
phys-org.description: Researchers monitoring online activity for six weeks in mid-2025 found primates, birds, snakes, frogs, orchids and many other wildlife groups advertised for sale across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube. Wildlife is increasingly being trafficked through online platforms. Online illegal wildlife trade poses significant risks to species, ecosystems, and animal and public health.

phys-org.title: Human rights rankings reveal surprising over- and underperformers
phys-org.description: When it comes to human rights, it probably won't surprise you that Scandinavian countries perform well by statistical measures, along with Canada and Australia. But did you know that Mozambique, the Philippines, and Rwanda are also considered "overperformers," meaning that they score higher on human rights than expected?

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
proj-syn.description: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still other

proj-syn.title: Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
proj-syn.description: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction. With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Gospel of the Great Leader
proj-syn.description: North Korea’s communist regime has long functioned as a faith, repurposing Christian doctrine and imagery to deify its founder, Kim Il-sung, and his descendants. A new book traces how those religious influences transformed the Kim dynasty’s personality cult into a system that has endured across three generations.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: Superintelligent Democracy
proj-syn.description: Rather than framing the pursuit of AI capabilities as a race, we should turn the process into a democratic mission, with milestones set by the people, rather than on their behalf. Taiwan's own demonstration of mission-led governance, along with insights from the open-web community, show what is possible.

proj-syn.title: How Europe Can Save a Trillion Euros and Win the AI Race
proj-syn.description: If the risk Europe faces is losing access to frontier AI models, the solution is not necessarily to chase the labs that created them in the hopes of eventually pulling ahead. Instead, it is to build the capacity to make surviving that loss possible, such as by investing in AI infrastructure and training capabilities.

proj-syn.title: MDBs Are Becoming a New Global Safe Asset
proj-syn.description: Even as multilateralism faces an existential threat, multilateral development banks are not only surviving but thriving. Thanks to MDBs’ ability to borrow at costs close to that of the US Treasury, they have created a new class of de facto risk-free assets that could help underpin the global financial system.

proj-syn.title: Why US Bond Markets Are Trembling
proj-syn.description: What is the apparent fragility in the US bond market telling us? Since markets tend to be less wrong than those who comment on them regularly, their signals must be taken seriously, especially when they coincide with a relative softening in US inflation figures and other high-frequency economic indicators.

proj-syn.title: Look East for Lessons in Democratic Resistance
proj-syn.description: Pro-democracy activists often turn to Eastern and Central Europe for inspiration, while Asia’s remarkable democratic breakthroughs receive far less attention. Yet the continent’s recent struggles offer valuable lessons for those seeking to resist the global advance of authoritarianism.

proj-syn.title: Three Ways AI Will Change the Course of Humanity
proj-syn.description: The AI debate has largely focused on productivity gains and job displacement, but its consequences will reach much further By revolutionizing how we combat disease, wage wars, and stimulate income growth, AI could fundamentally alter the terms of human existence.
